D: A gifted girl with neglectful parents discovers she has powers and takes on her terrifying headmistress.
P: Serve dessert when Bruce Bogtrotter faces the cake.
S: the Wormwoods eat in front of the TV every night

Crunchy panko chicken tenders with buttery mash, peas and a little pot of gravy, served on TV trays the way the Wormwoods like it. Cut 600g chicken tenderloins and dip in flour, 2 beaten eggs, then 150g panko. Lay on an oiled tray, spray with oil and bake at 220C for 18 minutes, turning once, until crisp. Boil 800g potatoes and mash with 60g butter and 80ml milk. Cook 300g frozen peas. Make gravy from a packet mix. Serve in sections on 4 trays.
Matilda reads every book in the library
Lavash cut into neat rectangles, brushed with oil and rosemary, baked at 180C until crisp, then stacked with slices of cheddar and apple like a pile of books.
tea at Miss Honey's tiny cottage
Self-raising flour with cold butter rubbed in, milk mixed in lightly with a knife, cut into rounds, packed close on the tray, baked at 220C for 12 minutes. Jam and cream.
M: Buttermilk batter rested 15 minutes, cooked in butter until bubbles set and the edges go lacy, stacked high with butter, maple syrup and blueberries warmed in a pan.
Harry Wormwood's car yard chilli dogs
Harry Wormwood's dodgy used car yard

Griddled franks in toasted buns, smothered in beef chilli and cheddar with jammy onions and mustard, a deal even Harry couldn't fiddle. Cook 2 sliced onions in 30g butter for 25 minutes until jammy. Brown 300g beef mince with 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp mild chilli powder and 200g passata and simmer 15 minutes. Simmer 8 franks 5 minutes, then sear on a griddle. Toast 8 hot dog buns. Fill each with a frank, chilli, onions, grated cheddar from 100g and a stripe of mustard.
W: the whole thing, in front of the school
Dark chocolate and butter melted, whisked with eggs, sugar and buttermilk, flour and cocoa folded in, baked at 170C for 45 minutes, covered in a thick fudge frosting. Slices, not the whole cake.
K: the newt in Miss Trunchbull's water jug

Fresh watermelon blitzed with lime and mint, strained over ice and topped with sparkling water in a big glass jug, no newts. Blend 1kg seedless watermelon flesh with the juice of 2 limes and a handful of mint until smooth. Strain into a large glass jug, pressing on the pulp. Add 1 tbsp honey if the melon is not very sweet and stir. Top with 500ml chilled sparkling water and plenty of ice. Pour into 4 glasses with mint sprigs.

s.note: Matilda reads every book in the library
s.how: Cut 2 lavash breads into neat rectangles, brush with oil, sprinkle with chopped rosemary and bake at 180C for 8 minutes until crisp. Cool, then stack with slices of 200g vintage cheddar and thin apple slices like a little pile of books.

s.note: tea at Miss Honey's tiny cottage
s.how: Rub 60g cold butter into 350g self-raising flour, then mix in 250ml milk lightly with a knife. Pat out, cut into rounds and pack close on a tray. Bake at 220C for 12 minutes. Serve warm with strawberry jam and 300ml whipped cream.

m.how: Whisk 300g flour, 2 tsp baking powder, 2 tbsp sugar, 500ml buttermilk and 2 eggs. Rest 15 minutes. Cook ladlefuls in butter until bubbles set. Warm 250g blueberries in a pan for 3 minutes. Stack high with butter, maple syrup and the blueberries.

w.note: the whole thing, in front of the school
w.how: Melt 200g dark chocolate with 200g butter. Whisk in 3 eggs, 250g sugar and 250ml buttermilk, then fold in 200g flour, 40g cocoa and 1 tsp bicarb. Bake at 170C for 45 minutes. Cover in frosting of 100g melted chocolate beaten with 100g butter and 150g icing sugar.
